properties.name: Hauert Lab — Swarm Engineering
properties.description:
**Sabine Hauert** — University of Bristol, Bristol (GB)

Professor of Swarm Engineering working across Engineering Mathematics, the Bristol Robotics Laboratory, and Life Sciences on 'swarms for people' across scales -- from nanoparticle swarms for cancer treatment (her earlier work at MIT) to larger robot swarms for environmental monitoring and logistics. Previously deployed flying robot swarms at EPFL. Also executive trustee of the AIhub.org and Robohub.org communities.

**Why it's on this map:** Swarm engineering spanning nanoparticle-scale medical applications to larger robot swarms -- a close match for anyone thinking about how many small autonomous agents coordinate as a group, medically and otherwise.

[[https://hauertlab.com/|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Winfree Lab — Molecular Robotics
properties.description:
**Erik Winfree** — California Institute of Technology, Pasadena, CA (US)

Pioneers DNA nanotechnology and molecular programming -- computation and robotics built from DNA itself rather than silicon. State-of-the-art DNA robots can walk a few steps along a 2D track, make branching decisions, and pick up cargo; the group is working toward molecular robots with swarm-intelligence-inspired collective behavior. Co-shared the 2006 Feynman Prize in Nanotechnology (with Paul Rothemund) for demonstrating DNA computing.

**Why it's on this map:** Pioneers molecular/DNA-based computation and robotics -- a completely different fabrication and computing substrate from silicon-based approaches, useful mainly as a conceptual reference point for what computing on board a molecule-scale device could even look like.

[[https://www.dna.caltech.edu/|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Electronic Vision(s) — Neuromorphic Computing Architectures
properties.description:
**Johannes Schemmel** — Heidelberg University, Heidelberg (DE)

Designs BrainScaleS, a mixed-signal analog/digital neuromorphic computing platform emulating spiking neural networks in continuous time (~1000x faster than biological real-time, far lower energy than conventional digital compute). BrainScaleS-2 integrates 512 adaptive integrate-and-fire neurons and 131k plastic synapses per chip; BrainScaleS-1 demonstrated wafer-scale neuromorphic integration. Part of the EU EBRAINS research infrastructure. PI Johannes Schemmel holds Heidelberg's Chair of Neuromorphic Computing Architectures and has led the group's ASIC lab since 2008.

**Why it's on this map:** Designs mixed-signal neuromorphic (spiking) hardware -- a real alternative-computing-substrate option relevant to how a tiny autonomous device's onboard intelligence, if any, might eventually be implemented.

[[https://www.kip.uni-heidelberg.de/vision/|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Heidemarie Schmidt Group
properties.description:
**Heidemarie Schmidt** — Leibniz Institute of Photonic Technology (IPHT Jena), Jena (DE)

Works on quantum detection and new detector systems characterizing quantum-limited signals, and on neuromorphic computing architectures based on memristive devices.

**Why it's on this map:** Works on memristive neuromorphic computing -- an alternative computing-hardware substrate, in the same family as other neuromorphic-hardware entries on this map.

[[https://www.leibniz-ipht.de/en/|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Self-Organizing Systems Research Group
properties.description:
**Radhika Nagpal** — Princeton University, Princeton, NJ (US)

Studies self-organizing computer systems, collective intelligence, and biologically-inspired multi-agent robotics. Created the Kilobots (published in Science, 2014): a swarm of 1,024 coin-sized, $14-each robots that self-assemble into arbitrary target shapes using only local sensing of immediate neighbors, no central controller. Radhika Nagpal moved the group from Harvard SEAS/Wyss to Princeton (Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering + Computer Science) in 2023.

**Why it's on this map:** A textbook example of collective swarm-behavior research (demonstrated at centimeter scale, not sub-millimeter) -- directly relevant to how many small autonomous agents might coordinate as a group.

[[https://ssr.princeton.edu/|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Jialin Jiang Group
properties.description:
**Jialin Jiang** — 沈阳自动化研究所, Shenyang (CN)

Works on microswarm path planning and navigation, including RRT*-based hybrid path planning for automatic navigation of microswarms -- vortex-like microswarms formed from millions of nanoscale Fe3O4 particles as the robot agents.

**Why it's on this map:** A microrobotics group at a major Chinese automation research institute -- direct categorical fit.

[[https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=zh-CN&q=Jialin+Jiang+microswarm|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: McCaskill Group — Evolutionary Biochemistry and Artificial Life
properties.description:
**John S. McCaskill** — Chemnitz University of Technology, Chemnitz (DE)

Works on the evolution of information processing across theoretical biochemistry, RNA/molecular evolution, microfluidics, microrobotics, and IT medical applications -- an "artificial life" framing of distributed intelligence and modular hardware. Led the earlier EU-funded project developing "lablets" (microscopic silicon chiplets) that became the building block for TU Chemnitz's recent "smartlet" modular microrobots (with Oliver Schmidt's group), which communicate via onboard optical signaling without external cameras, magnets, or antennas. Professor at Chemnitz University of Technology; previously Professor of Theoretical Biochemistry at Friedrich Schiller University Jena and guest professor at Ruhr University Bochum.

**Why it's on this map:** Approaches small-scale autonomous systems from the information-processing/artificial-life side rather than the actuation or fabrication side -- the underlying chiplet building block and communication-without-external-infrastructure design are a distinct, complementary angle on the same on-board-intelligence problem that a genuinely autonomous small robot has to solve, adjacent to but distinct from a pure hardware/materials contribution.

[[https://homepage.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/john.mccaskill/index.html|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown

properties.name: Xiang Cheng Group
properties.description:
**Xiang Cheng** — University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN (US)

Studies fluid dynamics, biophysics, and soft matter physics: swimming microorganisms in complex environments, collective dynamics of dense bacterial suspensions, rheology of colloidal suspensions, and emergent collective phenomena of granular robotic systems -- including directed transport of swimming bacteria through funnel-shaped obstacles as a model for rectifying living active matter.

**Why it's on this map:** Studies granular robotic swarms and active-matter physics -- an unusual-angle but real parallel to how many small autonomous agents might collectively behave.

[[https://cse.umn.edu/cems/xiang-cheng|Group website]]

Category: Information Technology · Smallest demonstrated: unknown
